finding.shortLabel: Fourteen further Norfolk John-Gurney baptisms across six parishes, 1623-1643, none matching the full child set

Mary Gurney, Denton, baptized 12 August 1638 (FS ID NNDF-V9K)
Robert Gvrney m. Mary Lame, 27 July 1622, Norwich (children Samuel bp.1623 St Stephen, Katherine bp.1639 St Benedict) - a Norfolk same-name household with a wife Mary, not the emigrant

finding.statement: A Findmypast UK Parish Baptisms search restricted to Norfolk, surname Gurney, father John, 1623-1643, returns fourteen further baptisms across six parishes: Denton (John + Rachell, children Mary 1638, Thomas 1639, Sarah 1644), Hempnall (Anna 1640, Elizabeth 1641), Stanfield (Mary 1634), Norwich St Margaret & St Swithin (a 1630 child), North Runcton (Beniamin 1625, Frances 1628), and Earsham (John + Elizabeth Singler). None of these six households reproduces the colonial John's full, distinctive child set -- Sarah, Mary, Richard, John Jr., and Peter -- by name and date, but the density is consistent with Norfolk having been a Gurney heartland with several parish-level Johns active in the same decade.

finding.shortLabel: John Gurnell (freeman 1643) is a distinct surname, confirmed by an 1675 Dorchester death entry

sources.locator: John Gurnell, application 10 May 1643, keyed to Colony Records vol. II, pp. 27-28

finding.statement: A separate 'John Gurnell,' admitted freeman in Massachusetts on 10 May 1643, is not John Gurney-1 under a different spelling. Surviving 1600s Massachusetts Gurnell records are thin enough to invite a Gurnell-to-Gurney misreading, but a 30 July 1675 Dorchester death entry, checked directly, reads 'Gurnell' plainly -- confirming Gurnell as its own surname. The colonial John is recorded under Gurney/Gurny/Garny variants throughout his New England career, never Gurnell.
